summary: Bilayer NbSe$_2$ coupled to a terahertz CSRR cavity shows a 10% enhancement of $T_c$ (from 3.02 K to 3.41 K) at 0.92 THz resonance, with the effect growing sharply in the two-dimensional limit and scaling roughly four times larger than in ten-layer devices. QED-DFT calculations show the enhancement arises from cavity-induced redistribution of spectral weight in the Eliashberg function, weakening electron-phonon coupling while hardening the logarithmic average phonon frequency, with the sign change in $T_c$ emerging from competition between these effects.
motivation: Cavity-induced modification of superconductivity has been theoretically predicted, but the microscopic mechanism and scaling with material dimensionality remain unknown.
method: Few-layer NbSe$_2$ flakes were coupled to a terahertz CSRR tuned to 0.92 THz, with $T_c$ and lower critical field measured spatially across the cavity field profile on a single continuous device; QED-DFT calculations tracked cavity-induced changes to the Eliashberg function.
result: Bilayer NbSe$_2$ shows $	riangle T_c = +0.39$ K at the cavity field maximum, decreasing to zero outside the resonator, with frequency-dependent non-monotonic response peaking near 0.96 THz; the effect is approximately four times larger in bilayers than in ten-layer NbSe$_2$ at the same cavity frequency.
